issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and introduction claim that the splitting removes the stiffness-induced time-step restriction and shows superior efficiency. The experiments are all run at CFL=0.1 with Δt∝Δx. The direct explicit DG method appears only as a reference solution. No test reports time-step sizes, step counts or CPU time for the explicit method versus the split scheme on the same problem. No test shows the explicit method failing or needing a much smaller step at this CFL. The split scheme has extra costs: three substeps, OE+BP limiting after every stage, bisection at every quadrature point, and the divergence reconstruction. The explicit transport step also still needs a CFL condition, and the paper gives no BP-CFL analysis for it. The efficiency gain is asserted, not established.

failure_location.quote: demonstrate the superior robustness and efficiency of the method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add comparisons of time-step size, step count or wall-clock time against the explicit Kapila DG on at least the water-air tests, or weaken the claim to robustness only.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised main benefit (efficiency, i.e. circumventing the severe CFL restriction) is unsupported. The numerical section shows only that the scheme runs and agrees with references.
issues.title: Efficiency / stiffness-removal advantage claimed but never tested
issues.why_classification: Repair needs new comparison experiments or withdrawal of a headline claim. Both are contained, but neither is a one-line routine fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The splitting steps are written with backward Euler, which is first order. The hybrid scheme recovers SDIRK2 only when the predictor lies in [0,1]. Otherwise it falls back to first-order backward Euler, which is exactly the stiff, near-bound regime that motivates the method. So O(Δt²) at the interface is not established. With Δt∝Δx, a genuinely second-order temporal error C·Δt² ~ Δx² must eventually dominate the O(Δx³) spatial error of P². An asymptotic third-order rate therefore cannot be 'expected'. The 'subdominant' statement is asserted without proof and is circular. The observed rates in the one smooth test (where κ-effects may be tiny) are pre-asymptotic evidence at best.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, the second-order limitation of Strang splitting is thus localized to the temporal precision at the two-phase interface

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that second order holds only where the SDIRK2 branch is active, and that the observed 3rd-order rate is pre-asymptotic for this test. Alternatively refine Δt faster than Δx to verify the spatial order.
issues.overall_effect: The stated temporal accuracy (second order at interfaces, high order elsewhere) and the claim that the DG(P^2) scheme is third-order accurate under Δt∝Δx are not supported by analysis.
issues.title: Claimed second-order temporal accuracy at interfaces and third-order convergence with Δt∝Δx unsupported
issues.why_classification: Rewording the claim, or adding a time-refinement test, preserves the method and its results. The source itself concedes local order degradation.

issues.failure_explanation: In (imkappa), ρe is frozen at level n while z_1 varies over [0,1], so p(z_1) is a fixed rational function of z_1. ν_k=1/(γ_k(p+p_{w,k})) and ν=z_1ν_1+z_2ν_2 can then vanish, change sign or blow up inside (0,1). The theorem assumes only z_1^n∈[0,1] and puts no hypothesis on ρe^n or p^n. Take the paper's own Appendix A data: ρe=3500.5, γ_1=1.4, p_{w,1}=0, γ_2=4.4, p_{w,2}=6000. At z_1=0 one has p=-2498.3 and ν=ν_2>0. At z_1=0.5 one has p=-273.3, p+p_{w,1}<0, and Wood's 1/(ρc²)=ν≈-0.00129<0. On [0,0.5] ν_1 and ν_2 are finite, so ν crosses 0 continuously. κ=z_1z_2(ν_1-ν_2)/ν has a genuine pole there, since the numerator stays negative. Hence f and F are not continuous on [0,1] and the intermediate-value argument fails. The theorem also proves only z_1^{n+1}∈[0,1] and gives no control of p^{n+1} (which changes with frozen ρe) or of the G^p property, yet the abstract and conclusion advertise 'unconditionally BP'. Only existence is shown, not uniqueness or a selection rule, although bisection is prescribed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add hypotheses (e.g. p(z_1)+p_{w,k}>0 for all z_1 in the search interval, or restriction to an admissible subinterval) under which κ is continuous. Prove the sign conditions at the interval ends. State clearly that only the z_1 bounds are guaranteed, and show or assume cell-average admissibility (p>0) after the κ step.
issues.overall_effect: The 'unconditionally BP' guarantee of the implicit κ-solver (and the SDIRK2 hybrid, whose BP proof is 'similar' and omitted) is not established in general. Scheme well-definedness and admissibility of the post-κ state in G^p are unproven for mixed cells with low ρe.
issues.title: Existence proof for implicit κ-step assumes continuity of f on [0,1] although frozen (ρe)^n makes ν and κ singular/sign-changing
issues.why_classification: A contained weakening with added hypotheses and an endpoint-sign argument is needed. This leaves a recognizably comparable result but is more than a routine local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: θ_p=(p(Ū)-ε_p)/(p(Ū)-min p(Ũ)) is the root of the chord of p between Ū and Ũ. It guarantees p≥ε_p at Ū+θ(Ũ-Ū) only if p is concave along the segment. Theorem 2.1 shows only that the numerator N(U)=E-|m|²/(2ρ)-Σz_kγ_kp_{w,k}/(γ_k-1) is concave. p=N/D with D=Σz_k/(γ_k-1) depending on z_1, so p itself is not concave. Only the superlevel set {N-εD≥0} is convex. Counterexample: γ_1=1.4, γ_2=4.4, zero momentum. Take Ū with z̄_1=0.1, N̄=1 (D̄≈0.515, p̄≈1.94). Take a Gauss-Lobatto value with z_1=0.9, N=-0.01 (D≈2.28, p≈-0.0044). Then ε_p=1e-13, θ_p≈0.9977, and N at θ_p is 1-1.01·0.9977≈-0.0077<0. The limited state has negative pressure, contradicting the claim that the limiter enforces (U_ingp).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define θ_p via the concave functional N(U)-ε_pD(U) (positive iff p>ε_p), using the concavity already shown in Theorem 2.1's proof, and take the chord root of that functional.
issues.overall_effect: The stated pressure-positivity guarantee of the BP limiter is not valid in two-phase cells where D differs between the average and the extremal point. The limiter step as written can output p<0.
issues.title: Pressure limiter θ_p uses a linear interpolation of p, which is not concave; positivity after limiting not guaranteed
issues.why_classification: A local redefinition of θ_p using an already-proved concave functional repairs the guarantee. Method, rates and scope are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: G is defined with strict inequalities z_1ρ_1>0 and z_2ρ_2>0. The counterexample's U^(1)=[1.2,0,0,1000,1] has z_2ρ_2=0 and U^(2)=[0,1000,0,6001,0] has z_1ρ_1=0. Neither belongs to G, so the appendix's 'Verification of U^(1), U^(2) ∈ G' is false as stated. The midpoint computation (p≈-273.3, Wood 1/(ρc²)≈-0.00129<0) is arithmetically correct but concerns a convex combination of two non-members, which does not show non-convexity of G.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the endpoints by nearby states with small positive partial densities and 0<z_1<1. Verify they lie in G, and note that c²<0 at the midpoint persists by continuity, or recompute it.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted non-convexity of G, the stated motivation for introducing G^p, is not demonstrated by the given example. Theorem 2.1's own proof is unaffected.
issues.title: Appendix A counterexample uses states that are not in the set G as defined
issues.why_classification: A short perturbation of the example plus a continuity remark fixes it. The claim and its motivation survive intact.
